title: A Baker lower bound on |3^o - 2^L| kills every Juggler near-convergent cycle length at a realistic floor
statement: There is a published effective lower bound on |3^o - 2^L| (Rhin / Laurent-Mignotte-Nesterenko / Simons-de Weger Lemma 12) such that, after substituting into n log n <= C L 3^o / (3^o - 2^L), every near-convergent Juggler cycle length is excluded by the Lean floor 53 or the computational floor 10^6.
counterexamples: L=19, o=12: exact gap 3^12 - 2^19 = 7153 already gives n_max ≈ 297 > 53, so the strongest possible lower bound fails at the Lean floor
Rhin/SdW Lemma 12 at L=19: squeeze against finance never fires at floors 53, 10^6, or 10^9
record lengths 84, 569, 1054, 25781, 50508: exact n_max grows along convergents of ln 2 / ln 3
mathematical_domain: Juggler cycle finance / linear forms in two logarithms
notes: Any correct gap lower bound is at most the exact gap, so it cannot exclude a length that exact finance keeps. Collatz gets an exponentially small upper bound on Lambda from m-cycle geometry; Juggler finance only gives |Lambda| <= O(L/(n log n)). Not the parked x^3 - y^2 campaign.
